maiasaura:enwiki:10.title: Maiasaura (Maiasaura and the popularisation of the "dinosaur renaissance")

facts.statement: Maiasaura was discovered in 1978 and formally described in 1979 by paleontologists Jack Horner and Bob Makela.
facts.quote: Discovered in 1978 during the dinosaur renaissance, the species description of Maiasaura first came in 1979 from paleontologists Jack Horner and Bob Makela

facts.statement: Evidence showed Maiasaura fed its young in the nest, marking the first known instance of parental care in dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Collected data at the site indicated that Maiasaura fed its young while they were in the nest, the first instance of parental and social behavior in dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Whole Maiasaura eggs were discovered in 1979, representing the first whole dinosaur eggs found in North America and the Western Hemisphere.
facts.quote: In 1979, one year after the discovery of the nests and juveniles, Maiasaura whole eggs were unearthed, the first discovery of dinosaur whole eggs both on the American continent and in the Western Hemisphere.

facts.statement: Maiasaura is the official state fossil of Montana.
facts.quote: Maiasaura, whose bones have been found by hundreds in the state of Montana, has been chosen as Montana's state fossil.

facts.statement: Maiasaura reached a maximum length of about 9 meters and a mass of up to 4 metric tons.
facts.quote: Maiasaura peeblesorum were large, attaining a maximum known length of about 9 m and an approximate body mass measured at up to 4 MT.

facts.statement: A prominent short, solid crest between the eyes distinguishes Maiasaura from other hadrosaurids.
facts.quote: While hadrosaurids have very similar post-cranial body plans, the distinguishing characteristic of Maiasaura peeblesorum is a prominent short, solid crest-like structure situated between the eyes.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the crest on Maiasaura may have been used for headbutting contests between males during breeding season.
facts.quote: This crest may have been used in headbutting contests between males during the breeding season.

facts.statement: Mass bone beds suggest Maiasaura herds could number as many as 10,000 individuals.
facts.quote: Mass bone beds discovered in the Two Medicine Formation show that herds could be extremely large and comprise as many as 10,000 individuals.

facts.statement: In 1978, paleontologist Bob Makela was contacted by Bill Clemens regarding bones found by a woman in northwestern Montana.
facts.quote: In 1978 paleontologist Bob Makela had been told by fellow Berkeley paleontologist Bill Clemens that the State of Montana had called him about a north-western Montana woman who had found bones which she wanted to identify.

facts.statement: In the summer of 1978, excavations at the site revealed a nest containing 15 baby dinosaurs without the need for digging.
facts.quote: There, bones were visible on the surface, not even needing to dig. During the same Summer of 1978, Makela and Horner excavated the spot and noticed that they were excavating a nest, where in the end they found a total of 15 baby dinosaurs.

facts.statement: In July 1979, student Fran Tannenbaum discovered the first whole dinosaur egg in North America and the Western Hemisphere.
facts.quote: The next year in July 1979, during the second summer dig, a lady student named Fran Tannenbaum, under the direction of Jack Horner, discovered the first whole dinosaur egg ever found in North America and in the Western Hemisphere.

facts.statement: The holotype skull specimen PU 22405 was discovered in 1979 by Laurie Trexler and is now housed at the Yale Peabody Museum.
facts.quote: A skull of Maiasaura, specimen PU 22405 (now in the collections of the Yale Peabody Museum of Natural History as YPM PU 22405 following the transfer of the Princeton University vertebrate paleontology collections), was discovered by David Trexler's wife Laurie Trexler in 1979.

facts.statement: The species name peeblesorum honors the families of John and James Peebles, who owned the land where fossils were found.
facts.quote: The specific name, peeblesorum, honours the families of John and James Peebles, on whose land the finds were made.

facts.statement: It is assumed that a volcanic eruption from the Elkhorn mountains covered nests, eggs, and animals in ash, leading to their near-perfect preservation.
facts.quote: It is assumed that such event was the eruption of a volcano located among the nearby Elkhorn mountains. Nests, eggs and animals were covered by ash and once they fossilised they remained almost perfectly preserved until they were discovered in 1978.

facts.statement: Maiasaura peeblesorum belongs to the tribe Brachylophosaurini alongside taxa such as Acristavus, Brachylophosaurus, Ornatops, and Probrachylophosaurus.
facts.quote: Maiasaura peeblesorum is in the tribe Brachylophosaurini along with these related taxa: Acristavus gagslarsoni Brachylophosaurus canadensis Ornatops incantatus Probrachylophosaurus bergei

facts.statement: Maiasaura lived in herds and raised its young in nesting colonies where nests were packed closely together with gaps of about 7 meters.
facts.quote: The nests in the colonies were packed closely together, like those of modern seabirds, with the gap between the nests being around 7 m

facts.statement: Maiasaura nests were made of earth and contained between 30 and 40 eggs arranged in a circular or spiral pattern.
facts.quote: The nests were made of earth and contained 30 to 40 eggs laid in a circular or spiral pattern

facts.statement: Fossilized Maiasaura peeblesorum eggs are black in color and feature high, prominent ridges on their outer surface.
facts.quote: Fossilized M. peeblesorum eggs are black in color and have high, prominent ridges on the outer surface

facts.statement: Maiasaura parents incubated their eggs using heat from rotting vegetation placed in the nest instead of sitting on them.
facts.quote: The eggs were incubated by the heat resulting from rotting vegetation placed into the nest by the parents, rather than a parent sitting on the nest

facts.statement: Baby Maiasaura hatched with undeveloped legs, making them incapable of walking immediately.
facts.quote: Upon hatching, fossils of baby Maiasaura show that their legs were not fully developed and thus they were incapable of walking

facts.statement: Worn teeth on juvenile Maiasaura fossils indicate that adults brought food to the nest for them.
facts.quote: Fossils also show that their teeth were partly worn, which means that the adults brought food to the nest

facts.statement: Maiasaura hatchlings grew from 16 to 58 inches in length during their first year.
facts.quote: The hatchlings grew from a size of 16 to 58 in long in the span of their first year

facts.statement: Research suggests infant Maiasaura were altricial and left their nests after 40 to 75 days.
facts.quote: Based on metabolic growth rates and age estimations of juvenile specimens both in and outside the nests, it is suggested that infant Maiasaura were altricial and left the confines of their nests after 40-75 days

facts.statement: If Maiasaura survived their second year, their mortality rate dropped to 12.7%.
facts.quote: If the animals survived their second year, their mortality rate would drop to 12.7%

facts.statement: Maiasaura reached sexual maturity in their third year and skeletal maturity at eight years of age.
facts.quote: Sexual maturity was found to occur in their third year, while skeletal maturity was attained at eight years of age

facts.statement: Maiasaura included rotting wood in its diet and lived in an environment with a long, dry season prone to drought.
facts.quote: It was also found that Maiasaura also included rotting wood in its diet, as well that its environment had a long, dry season prone to drought

facts.statement: Dental wear analysis shows juvenile Maiasaura peeblesorum had more crush wear than adults, who displayed more shear wear.
facts.quote: Analysis of its dental wear patterns show that juvenile M. peeblesorum exhibited more crush wear than adults, which displayed more shear wear than juveniles

facts.statement: Studies by Saitta et al. suggest one sex of Maiasaura was roughly 45% larger than the other based on size statistics.
facts.quote: Studies of Maiasaura by Saitta et al., suggest that one sex was roughly 45% larger than the other according to the mathematical analysis known as size statistics

facts.statement: In the Oldman Formation of Alberta, Maiasaura lived alongside ceratopsians such as Albertaceratops, Anchiceratops, Chasmosaurus, Coronosaurus, and Wendiceratops.
facts.quote: In the Oldman Formation of Alberta, Maiasaura lived alongside the ceratopsians Albertaceratops, Anchiceratops, Chasmosaurus, Coronosaurus, and Wendiceratops

facts.statement: The genus Maiasaura was described by Horner and Makela in 1979.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Horner & Makela, 1979

facts.statement: The species Maiasaura peeblesorum was described by Horner and Makela in 1979.
facts.quote: species_authority: Horner & Makela, 1979

facts.statement: Maiasaura peeblesorum is the only known species in the extinct genus Maiasaura.
facts.quote: Maiasaura peeblesorum es la única especie conocida del género extinto Maiasaura

facts.statement: Maiasaura was an ornithopod hadrosaurid dinosaur.
facts.quote: de dinosaurio ornitópodo hadrosáurido

facts.statement: Maiasaura lived during the late Upper Cretaceous period, approximately between 76.7 and 70.6 million years ago in the Campanian stage.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico superior, hace aproximadamente entre 76,7 y 70,6 millones de años, en el Campaniense

facts.statement: Maiasaura lived in what is now North America.
facts.quote: en lo que es hoy Norteamérica

facts.statement: Dozens of nests were found at the site now known as Egg Mountain alongside Maiasaura fossils.
facts.quote: Junto a los restos descubiertos se encontraron decenas de nidos en el yacimiento hoy en día llamado Egg Mountain

facts.statement: The Egg Mountain site where Maiasaura nests were found is located in Montana, USA.
facts.quote: en Montana, Estados Unidos

facts.statement: Maiasaura fossils provided the first evidence that non-avian dinosaurs fed their young.
facts.quote: Ésta fue la primera prueba de que los dinosaurios no aviares alimentaban a sus crías

facts.statement: Maiasaura measured around 9 meters in length and weighed nearly 3 tonnes.
facts.quote: Maiasaura medía alrededor de 9 metros de longitud con un peso de casi 3 toneladas

facts.statement: Maiasaura had a flat beak typical of hadrosaurids and thick noses.
facts.quote: Tenían un pico plano típico de los hadrosáuridos y narices gruesas

facts.statement: Maiasaura possessed a small pointed crest in front of the eyes.
facts.quote: Tenían una pequeña cresta puntiaguda frente a los ojos

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the eye crest may have been used in head-butting contests between males during the breeding season.
facts.quote: Esta cresta puede haber sido utilizada en concursos de cabezazos entre machos durante la temporada de reproducción

facts.statement: Maiasaura was a herbivore.
facts.quote: Maiasaura era herbívoro

facts.statement: Maiasaura could walk on two legs (bipedally) or four legs (quadrupedally).
facts.quote: Era capaz de caminar sobre dos patas, bípedos o cuatro cuadrúpedos

facts.statement: Bone stress pattern studies show that juveniles under 4 years old walked primarily bipedally, switching to a primarily quadrupedal style as they grew.
facts.quote: Los estudios de los patrones de estrés de los huesos curados muestran que los jóvenes menores de 4 años caminaban principalmente bípedos, cambiando a un estilo de caminar principalmente cuadrúpedo cuando crecieron

facts.statement: Maiasaura likely lacked defenses against predators except perhaps for a heavy muscular tail and herd behavior.
facts.quote: Parecían no tener defensa contra los depredadores, excepto, quizás, su pesada cola muscular y su comportamiento de rebaño

facts.statement: Maiasaura herds could have been extremely large, potentially comprising up to 10,000 individuals.
facts.quote: Los rebaños eran extremadamente grandes y podrían haber comprendido hasta 10 000 individuos

facts.statement: Maiasaura lived in an interior habitat.
facts.quote: Maiasaura vivía en un hábitat interior

facts.statement: The holotype skull specimen PU 22405 was discovered by Laurie Trexler in 1979 and is now housed at the Yale Peabody Museum.
facts.quote: Un cráneo de Maiasaura, el espécimen PU 22405, ahora en las colecciones del Museo de Historia Natural de Yale Peabody como YPM PU 22405 tras la transferencia de las colecciones de paleontología de vertebrados de la Universidad de Princeton, fue descubierto por Laurie Trexler en 1979

facts.statement: Jack Horner and Robert Makela described the specimen as the holotype of a new species.
facts.quote: y descrito por los paleontólogos de dinosaurios Jack Horner y Robert Makela como el holotipo de una nueva especie

facts.statement: The species was named Maiasaura peeblesorum.
facts.quote: Llamaron a la especie tipo Maiasaura peeblesorum

facts.statement: The generic name Maiasaura refers to the Greek goddess Maia, the "Good Mother," using the feminine form of saurus.
facts.quote: El nombre genérico se refiere a la diosa griega Maia, la "Buena Madre", para enfatizar esto, utilizaron la forma femenina de saurus, saura

facts.statement: The specific name peeblesorum honors the families of John and James Peebles, whose land yielded the fossils.
facts.quote: El nombre específico honra a las familias de John y James Peebles, en cuya tierra se hicieron los hallazgos

facts.statement: The generic name references Marion Brandvold's 1978 discovery of a nest containing eggshell fragments and babies too large to be hatchlings.
facts.quote: El nombre genérico se refiere al descubrimiento de Marion Brandvold en 1978 de un nido con restos de cáscaras de huevo y bebés demasiado grandes para ser crías

facts.statement: These discoveries led to the area being known as "Egg Mountain" in the Two Medicine Formation near Choteau in western Montana.
facts.quote: Estos descubrimientos llevaron a otros y el área se hizo conocida como "Montaña del Huevo", en rocas de la Formación Dos Medicinas cerca de Choteau en el oeste de Montana

facts.statement: More than 200 specimens of Maiasaura have been found, representing all age ranges.
facts.quote: Se han encontrado más de 200 especímenes, de todos los rangos de edad

facts.statement: The closest phylogenetic relative of the genus Maiasaura appears to be Brachylophosaurus.
facts.quote: La relación filogenética más cercana del género Maiasaura parece corresponder con Brachylophosaurus

facts.statement: Maiasaura was recently placed in a new clade called Brachylophosaurini along with Brachylophosaurus and Acristavus.
facts.quote: Recientemente, junto con Brachylophosaurus y Acristavus, fue situado en un nuevo clado llamado Brachylophosaurini

facts.statement: Experts believe Maiasaura lived in enormous nomadic herds that annually returned to the same nesting site due to the large number of nests and skeletons found in North America.
facts.quote: Debido a la gran cantidad de nidos y esqueletos encontrados en Norteamérica, los expertos creen que los maiasaura vivían en enormes manadas nómadas, que anualmente regresaban al mismo lugar de reproducción

facts.statement: It is possible that Maiasaura nests were reused from one year to the next.
facts.quote: Es posible que los nidos fueran reutilizados de un año a otro

facts.statement: Maiasaura was contemporary with Orodromeus, Troodon, the ceratopsid Centrosaurus, the armored Euoplocephalus, and earlier relatives of the tyrannosaur Daspletosaurus and Gorgosaurus.
facts.quote: El Maiasauria fue contemporáneo al Orodromeus, Troodon, el ceratópsido Centrosaurus, el macizo Euoplocephalus y parientes más tempranos del tiranosaurio, el Daspletosaurus y Gorgosaurus

facts.statement: Maiasaura lacked powerful weapons to deter predators, so they likely used flight or camouflage as a strategy.
facts.quote: Estos animales no estaban dotados con poderosas armas para repeler a los depredadores, por lo que probablemente utilizaran la huida o el camuflaje como estrategia

facts.statement: It is possible that Maiasaura possessed highly developed hearing and vision to detect intruders.
facts.quote: Es posible que poseyeran los sentidos del oído y la vista muy desarrollados para descubrir a los intrusos

facts.statement: Maiasaura fed on plants, leaves, fruits, and seeds.
facts.quote: Se alimentaba de plantas, hojas, frutas y semillas

facts.statement: Maiasaura's duck-bill shaped beak had several rows of teeth in the back of the mouth that crushed food after it was cut by the beak.
facts.quote: Su hocico, con forma de pico de pato típica de los hadrosáuridos poseía varias hileras de dientes en la parte posterior de la boca que trituraban el alimento una vez se cortaba con el pico

facts.statement: An adult Maiasaura had to eat 90 kg of vegetation to maintain good health.
facts.quote: Un adulto tenía que comer 90 kg de vegetales para poder tener buena salud

facts.statement: Maiasaura nests were very close together, similar to modern birds, with a space of around 7 meters between them, less than the length of an adult.
facts.quote: Los nidos estaban muy cerca uno del otro, como en las aves modernas actuales, con un espacio entre los nidos de alrededor de 7 metros, menos que el largo de un adulto

facts.statement: Maiasaura excavated a hole in the ground 2 meters in diameter with a crater-like shape.
facts.quote: Maiasaura excavaba en el suelo un hueco de 2 m de diámetro con forma de cráter

facts.statement: These earth nests contained between 30 to 40 eggs each in a circular or spiral pattern.
facts.quote: Estos nidos estaban hechos de tierra y contenían cada uno entre 30 a 40 huevos en un patrón circular o espiralado

facts.statement: Maiasaura eggs were approximately the size of ostrich eggs.
facts.quote: Los huevos son de aproximadamente el tamaño de los huevos de un avestruz

facts.statement: Maiasaura eggs were incubated by the heat from decomposing vegetation placed in the nest by parents, rather than by a parent brooding them.
facts.quote: Los huevos fueron incubados por el calor resultante de la vegetación en descomposición puesta en el nido por los padres, en vez de que un padre los empollara sentándose en el nido

facts.statement: Maiasaura baby fossils show their legs were not fully developed and they were unable to walk.
facts.quote: Los fósiles de maiasauras bebé demuestran que sus piernas no eran completamente desarrolladas y eran incapaces de caminar

facts.statement: Fossils show Maiasaura babies used their teeth, indicating adults brought food to the nest.
facts.quote: Los fósiles también demuestran usaron sus dientes, así que significa que los adultos trajeron el alimento al nido

facts.statement: Maiasaura chicks grew from 41 to 147 centimeters in length within their first year.
facts.quote: Las crías crecían de 41 a 147 centímetros de largo en el plazo de su primer año

facts.statement: At this point, or perhaps after another year, the animal left the nest.
facts.quote: A este punto, o quizás después de otro año, el animal abandonaba el nido

facts.statement: This high growth rate may be considered evidence that Maiasaura possessed warm blood.
facts.quote: Esta alta tasa de crecimiento puede ser considerado como una prueba de que poseían sangre caliente

facts.statement: Chicks had different facial proportions than adults, with larger eyes and shorter snouts.
facts.quote: Las crías tenían diversas proporciones faciales de los adultos, con ojos más grandes y un hocico más corto

facts.statement: When mating, this ornithopod built a nest and laid between 18 and 30 eggs, waiting until they hatched.
facts.quote: Este ornitópodo cuando se apareaba, después hacia un nido en el que ponía entre 18 y 30 huevos y esperaba hasta que nacieran

facts.statement: During incubation, babies measured 50 cm in length and had light bones, long weak limbs, an arched spine, and a U-shaped neck similar to adults.
facts.quote: Durante la incubación, los bebés medían 50 cm de longitud y tenían huesos ligeros, extremidades largas y débiles, columna vertebral arqueada y cuello en forma de U semejante al de los adultos

facts.statement: Small individuals remained in the nest because their weak legs prevented them from running or walking.
facts.quote: Los individuos pequeños permanecían siempre en el nido porque sus patas débiles les impedían correr o caminar

facts.statement: Another task for the Maiasaura mother was bringing food to the chicks, which could not collect it themselves.
facts.quote: Otro trabajo que tenía que encargarse la madre maiasauria era llevarles alimento al nido a los crías, las cuales no podían recolectarlo

facts.statement: However, their teeth were worn, indicating prolonged parental care.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, sus dientes estaban desgastados, lo que indica un cuidado parental prolongado

facts.statement: Parents likely chewed hard plants to facilitate food for their young.
facts.quote: Probablemente los padres masticaban las plantas duras para facilitarles el alimento a sus crías

facts.statement: It has been speculated that adults may have taken turns guarding the nest.
facts.quote: También se ha especulado con la posibilidad que los adultos hicieran turnos de vigilancia

facts.statement: Maiasaura chicks stayed in the nest for two years.
facts.quote: La cría permanecía en el nido por 2 años.

facts.statement: Maiasaura babies grew very fast, doubling their length in just four weeks.
facts.quote: Los bebés crecían muy rápido, duplicaban su longitud en tan solo cuatro semanas.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence shows Maiasaura was ready to leave the nest and join the herd at approximately 1.5 meters long.
facts.quote: Por medio de fósiles se ha descubierto que cuando alcanzaba aproximadamente 1,5 m de largo ya estaba listo para abandonar el nido y unirse a la manada.

facts.statement: By the age of two, Maiasaura reached lengths of 3 meters.
facts.quote: Ya cuando el maiasauria tenía 2 años de edad, alcanzaba longitudes de 3 m.

facts.statement: Maiasaura reached adulthood between 4 and 6 years of age.
facts.quote: Pero ya llegaba a la edad adulta cuando tenía entre 4 y 6 años.

facts.statement: Female Maiasaura likely returned to nest in the same location every year, sometimes with up to 10,000 other animals.
facts.quote: Al parecer la maiasauria hembra regresaba a anidar cada año al mismo lugar, hasta con 10000 animales más.

facts.statement: Analysis of fifty individual Maiasaura tibias revealed a mortality rate of approximately 89.9% in their first year of life.
facts.quote: A partir de una muestra de cincuenta tibias individuales de Maiasaura, se descubrió que tenían una tasa de mortalidad de aproximadamente el 89,9% en su primer año de vida.

facts.statement: In their eighth year and beyond, the mortality rate for Maiasaura rose again to around 44.4%.
facts.quote: En su octavo año y más allá, la tasa de mortalidad de Maiasaura volvería a subir a alrededor del 44,4%.

facts.statement: Maiasaura lived in an environment with a long, drought-prone dry season.
facts.quote: También se descubrió que Maiasaura también incluía madera podrida en su dieta, así como que su entorno tenía una estación seca larga y propensa a la sequía.

facts.statement: Maiasaura were primarily bipedal as juveniles but shifted to a more quadrupedal posture as they aged.
facts.quote: Los estudios que siguieron también encontraron que los Maiasaura eran principalmente bípedos como juveniles, y cambiaron a una postura más cuadrúpeda a medida que envejecían.

facts.statement: The study results were published in the journal Paleobiology on September 3, 2015.
facts.quote: Los resultados del estudio fueron publicados en la revista Paleobiología el 3 de septiembre de 2015.

facts.statement: Hunter & Janis (2026) reported evidence that Maiasaura shifted from feeding on nutritious, low-fiber plants to nutritionally poor, high-fiber plants during its life.
facts.quote: Hunter & Janis (2026) compare tooth wear in juvenile and adult individuals of Maiasaura peeblesorum, and report evidence of differences interpreted as consistent with a shift from feeding on nutritious, low-fiber plants to feeding on nutritionally poor, high-fiber plants during the life of the studied dinosaur.

facts.statement: Maiasaura is a characteristic fossil of the middle portion, lithofacies 4, of the Two Medicine Formation, dating to approximately 76.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Maiasaura es un fósil característico de la porción media, litofacies 4, de la Formación Dos Medicamentos, que data de hace aproximadamente 76,4 millones de años.

facts.statement: The discovery of the additional hadrosaurid Gryposaurus latidens in the same range as Maiasaura showed that the boundary between hypothetical upper and middle faunas was less distinct than previously thought.
facts.quote: El descubrimiento de un hadrosáurido adicional, Gryposaurus latidens, en el mismo rango que Maiasaura ha demostrado que el límite entre las faunas distintas hipotéticas en la parte superior y media es menos distinto de lo que se pensaba.

facts.statement: The genus Maiasaura was named by Horner and Makela in 1979.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Maiasaura (genus), Horner and Makela 1979

facts.statement: Maiasaura belongs to the parent group Brachylophosaurini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Brachylophosaurini

facts.statement: Maiasaura is classified in the family Hadrosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Hadrosauridae

facts.statement: Maiasaura is classified in the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Maiasaura lived during the Campanian stage, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: It is incorrect to associate Maiasaura with the ceratopsid Einiosaurus in a single fauna, as Maiasaura is known exclusively from older strata.
facts.quote: Mientras que Maiasaura históricamente se ha asociado con la formación Dos Medicinas con el ceratópsido Einiosaurus en una sola fauna, esto es incorrecto, ya que Maiasaura se conoce exclusivamente de estratos más antiguos.
